Payment reminder email for landscapers

Landscaping bills differently from most trades: season invoices, deposits, snow and HOAs. Here is a reminder schedule and wording that fit.

Checked 2026-11-21. Menus in other products change, so a label may differ slightly on your screen.

Short answer: send a friendly reminder on or just before the due date, an overdue email about a week later, a firmer one at two to three weeks, and a final notice near 30 days. Landscaping has its own wrinkles: monthly season billing, deposits on installs, snow invoices, HOAs that pay on a board cycle, and customers who go quiet when the season ends. Time your reminders around those.

Why landscaping invoices run late

Often a landscaping invoice is late not because the customer is refusing to pay, but because the work is easy to forget. A mowing visit is quick, the customer is at work, and nothing about it feels like a bill. Then fall arrives, the visits stop, and so does the habit of paying.

The fix is a schedule that matches the way you bill, plus wording you can send without thinking about it.

A reminder schedule for each type of job

Seasonal maintenance billed monthly

Send one invoice at the start or end of each month and give it 14 days. Remind the customer 3 days before the due date, again 7 days after, and again 21 days after. If the invoice is a month of visits, name the month and the property so it is clear what is being paid for. This is the one most worth automating, because the same message goes to many customers every month.

One-off installs with a deposit

For a patio, planting or sod job, the deposit should be paid before you order materials or book a crew. Do not wait a week to chase it. Send a reminder 1 to 2 days after the due date and say plainly that the start date depends on it. For the final balance, remind on the due date, then 7 and 14 days after. A customer who has a finished yard in front of them is the easiest person to collect from, so do it fast.

Snow removal

Snow invoices come in several shapes: per push, per event, or one price for the season, sometimes split into monthly payments. Per-push customers get an invoice after a storm and often question the count, so attach the dates and times of each visit. Seasonal customers on a monthly plan follow the same schedule as monthly mowing. Either way, remind early. Snow work is billed in the middle of a busy week and gets buried.

HOAs and property managers

These customers rarely pay the day an invoice arrives. A manager may need approval, or the board may only pay on certain dates. Ask at the start of the contract how and when they pay, who approves invoices, and whether they need a purchase order number or a particular invoice format. Then time your reminders to match. If the board meets on the second Tuesday, make sure your invoice is in the packet before it. Send reminders to the manager and, if you have been given the address, the accounts payable contact, not to a board member.

End of season

This is where money is easiest to lose. The last visit is done, the yard is out of sight, and the customer has moved on to other things. Send your final seasonal invoices as soon as the last visit is done, not in a batch at year end, and reduce the gaps between reminders. A good rule is to have every season invoice reminded by the time you plan next year's schedule. If a customer is still unpaid when you send renewal pricing, say that the account needs to be settled first.

Wording you can copy

Each of these fits a typical job. Change the details in the square brackets before you send.

1. Friendly, on or before the due date (monthly mowing)

Subject: Invoice [invoice number] for [month] lawn service, due [due date] Hi [name], Your invoice [invoice number] for [amount] covers our visits at [property address] in [month]. It is due on [due date]. A copy is attached. You can pay online here: [pay link] Thank you for having us out this season. [your name] [your company] | [phone]

2. Overdue (a week or so late)

Subject: Invoice [invoice number] - a quick reminder Hi [name], Invoice [invoice number] for [amount] was due on [due date] and I don't see a payment yet. It covers [work, for example the April to June mowing visits]. A copy is attached. You can pay here: [pay link] If a check is already in the mail, thank you, and please ignore this. If anything on the invoice looks wrong, tell me and I will fix it. [your name] [your company] | [phone]

3. Firmer (two to three weeks late, work still going on)

Subject: Invoice [invoice number] is [days] days overdue Hi [name], Invoice [invoice number] for [amount] was due on [due date]. We have kept up our visits at [property address], and the balance is still open. Please let me know by [date] when we can expect payment, or call me on [phone] if you would like to talk it over. We will [keep the next scheduled visit / hold the next visit] until we hear from you. You can pay here: [pay link] [your name] [your company]

4. Final notice (about 30 days late)

Subject: Final notice: invoice [invoice number] Hi [name], Invoice [invoice number] for [amount] is now [days] days overdue, and I have not had a reply to my earlier emails. Please pay by [date]. If we have not heard from you by then, we will [stop service at the property / add the late fee in our service agreement / send the account to collections]. I would rather settle this directly, so please call me on [phone] today. [your name] [your company]

Only name a consequence you are willing to carry out. Late fees and what you can do about unpaid work depend on your written agreement and your state's law, so check both. This is not legal advice. For more on how to word and sequence these, see how to chase overdue invoices by email, and for timing in general, how often to send invoice reminders.

A short text message

Many customers see a text sooner than an email, and landscaping crews already text customers about visit times. Use one only for customers who have agreed to receive texts from you, and stop right away if someone says stop. Keep it to billing and leave out any sales pitch.

Hi [name], it's [your name] at [your company]. Invoice [invoice number] for [amount] is past due. Pay here: [pay link]. Questions? Call [phone]. Reply STOP to opt out.

Doing it with QuickBooks Online

If you invoice from QuickBooks Online, go to Settings, then Account and settings, then Sales. In the Reminders section, click Edit, turn on Automatic invoice reminders, and set up to three reminders before or after the due date. QuickBooks sends them only for invoices you have already emailed, and everyone gets the same wording. That is fine for monthly mowing. It is not enough when an HOA needs a different message than a homeowner, or when a customer has a dispute and should be left alone. The standard reminders cannot leave one customer out. QuickBooks Online Advanced can, using workflows. See how to stop QuickBooks invoice reminders for one customer.

Check before you send

  • Look for a payment that arrived this morning, especially checks the office has not yet deposited.
  • Skip customers in a dispute, such as a lawn that did not recover or a disputed snow count.
  • Do not send a reminder to a customer you emailed yesterday.
